from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "Words change meaning based on neighbors.",

        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Problem: Contextual Ambiguity", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations

        self.play(Create(arrow_to_river), Create(arrow_to_money))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFB6C1"))
        ambiguity_ring = Annulus(inner_radius=0.3, outer_radius=0.4, color="#FF0000")
        ambiguity_ring.move_to(word_bank.get_center())
        
        self.play(ShowPassingFlash(ambiguity_ring, run_time=2, rate_func=there_and_back))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Attention is a matrix of similarity scores.",
            "Dot products turn queries and keys into scores.",
            "Softmax transforms scores into importance probabilities.",
            "High intensity shows strong attention relationships.",
            "Low intensity shows weak attention relationships."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Score: The Softmax Heatmap", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create 5x5 grid
        grid_group = VGroup()
        for i in range(5):
            for j in range(5):
                rect = Square(side_length=0.9, fill_opacity=0.3, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
                grid_group.add(rect)
        grid_group.arrange_in_grid(rows=5, cols=5, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(grid_group, 'A2', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Add labels
        q_label = Text("Queries", font_size=20).next_to(grid_group, LEFT)
        k_label = Text("Keys", font_size=20).next_to(grid_group, UP)
        self.add(q_label, k_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        formula = MathTex(r"\text{Softmax}(x_i) = \frac{e^{x_i}}{\sum e^{x_j}}", font_size=24).to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        # Highlight a "high" intensity cell (e.g., 0,0)
        grid_group[0].set_fill("#FF4500", opacity=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#1E90FF"))
        # Highlight a "low" intensity cell (e.g., 4,4)
        grid_group[24].set_fill("#1E90FF", opacity=0.3)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students with basic computer science knowledge

sections.title: The Problem: Contextual Ambiguity
sections.content: Introduce the challenge of language: words change meaning based on their neighbors. We need a mechanism that doesn't just read linearly, but 'looks' at the whole sentence at once.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' what does 'it' refer to? An animal or the street? A human knows it's the animal.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Query, Key, and Value
sections.content: Explain the database analogy: Query (Q) is what I'm looking for, Key (K) is the label of information available, and Value (V) is the actual content. We compute a similarity score between Q and K to weight the importance of V.
sections.example: Imagine a library: You have a search query (Q). The book titles on the shelf are Keys (K). The actual information inside the books is the Value (V). You pay more attention to books with matching titles.

sections.title: Visualizing the Score: The Softmax Heatmap
sections.content: Represent the attention mechanism as a matrix. Use a grid visualization where rows are queries and columns are keys. The dot product (Q·Kᵀ) creates a score, and Softmax turns these into probabilities (weights), visually shown as a color intensity gradient.
sections.example: A 5x5 grid where the intersection of 'it' and 'animal' glows bright red (high weight), while 'it' and 'street' remains cool blue (low weight).

sections.title: Multi-Head Attention: Parallel Perspectives
sections.content: Explain that one 'look' isn't enough. By using multiple 'heads,' the model can attend to different aspects simultaneously: one head looks at grammar, another at subject-verb agreement, and another at emotional context.
sections.example: Imagine 8 researchers reading the same document. One looks for names, one for locations, and one for logical contradictions, combining their findings into a comprehensive report.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap how the Transformer abandons sequential processing (like RNNs) in favor of this parallel attention mechanism, allowing it to scale to the massive LLMs we see today.
sections.example: Just as a spotlight highlights a performer on a dark stage, the Attention Mechanism allows the AI to focus its 'computational power' on the most relevant tokens regardless of where they appear in the text.
